messages:
maya: Heads up — provisioning for the new GPU fleet in us-east-1 is failing. Lots of CreateSecurityGroup / AuthorizeSecurityGroupIngress 429s. Affects multi-account onboarding runs.

david: Saw the same. Failed during parallel account bootstrap, ~40% of attempts got RequestLimitExceeded.

li: Error excerpt from kube-provisioner logs: 
```
AWSRequestError: RequestLimitExceeded: request rate too high
status code: 429, request id: abc-123
command: aws ec2 create-security-group --group-name rwd-ephemeral-123
```
We’re creating an ephemeral SG per pod per account — that pattern will hit the API hard.

ashley: Oof. We’ve been doing 50 concurrent creates across 8 accounts when onboarding capacity.

maya: Immediate mitigation: switch to pre-provisioned shared SGs per account (or reuse a small pool) and throttle the bootstrap to 5-10 parallel creates. Can someone push a small change to the bootstrap job?

david: I can patch the provisioner today to reuse a per-account sg pool + backoff. Will add jitter and exponential backoff (retry after 200ms, 500ms, 1s, 2s).

li: Also suggests batching network rules into fewer AuthorizeSecurityGroupIngress calls instead of many small ones. That cut our rate by ~70% in a staging test.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: Started rollout: provisioner-reuse-sg-pool v1.1 -> canary on us-east-1. Monitor for 15m.

maya: Good — parallel ask to Cloud Ops: we should open a support case with AWS to increase EC2 API request limits for CreateSecurityGroup/AuthorizeSecurityGroup in us-east-1 across our org accounts. This is hitting us across 6 linked accounts.

aws-support-bot: AWS case created: 1234567891. Case notes: Request for higher EC2 security group API rate for org unit "redwood-prod" in us-east-1. Support assigned.

ashley: For the ticket we need concrete numbers: current observed RPS per account (~12 rps bursts), desired soft limit (25 rps), planned steady state after mitigation (<=8 rps). I'll collect metrics from CloudWatch.

li: FYI there’s also a per-region limit on security group rule numbers that could bite us if we create too many unique SGs. We should not create SG-per-pod long term.

maya: Agreed. Long-term plan: 1) reuse SG pool, 2) use tags and port-based rule templating, 3) move ephemeral isolation into overlay network where possible.

david: Quick cost note — keeping thousands of ephemeral SGs around increases management complexity but not direct cost. The bigger cost is failed provisioning + manual retries delaying GPU onboarding (we lost a 3-hour window during yesterday’s scale test).

ashley: Action items: david to submit PR for reuse+backoff (ETA 3h), maya to coordinate with Cloud Ops to collect CW metrics and update AWS case, ops to hold off large multi-account bulk onboarding until canary proves green.

maya: Adding the JIRA: INFRA-4823 created to track changes and follow-up. Link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INFRA-4823

david: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood/provisioner/pull/789 — includes pool + backoff + batching of rule writes.

ops-bot: monitor-bot: Canary looks healthy for 12 minutes (no 429 spikes), will continue to watch for 1h.

maya: If AWS agrees to a temporary API increase, we’ll still keep reuse logic. Rising limits only helps during peak onboarding, not daily steady state.

ashley: Will follow up with finance if we need to accelerate cross-account support plan (some accounts need Business Support to raise these quotas).

li: One more note — region constraint: us-east-1 is hot. Consider moving part of onboarding to us-east-2 for future runs; that region currently shows lower SG API utilization.

maya: Thanks all. Please post any anomalies in this thread. If you’re on call, ping me directly for escalation. :thumbsup:
